page.metaDescription: A Crayon alternative for small teams. Track competitor pricing, product launches and hiring with watchlists and a weekly AI brief. Self-serve, monthly plans from $29.
page.h1: A Crayon alternative for small teams
page.subtitle: Crayon tracks competitors for go-to-market teams at larger companies. WebMonitor covers the core of it, knowing what changed on competitor websites each week, for small teams on a monthly plan.
page.intro: Crayon is a long-established competitive intelligence platform. It collects changes and news about competitors, scores them for importance, and delivers intel and battlecards into Salesforce, Slack and sales tools. It is sold through a sales process, and buyers report contracts from about $12,700 to $46,000 a year, plus onboarding fees. If your team is a founder, a product marketer or a small sales team, much of that platform goes unused. WebMonitor watches the competitor pages that matter and writes up the week for you.

features.title: Pages found for you
features.body: Give WebMonitor a competitor's domain and it suggests their pricing, changelog, blog, careers and integrations pages from their sitemap and navigation.

features.title: Noise filtered by AI
features.body: Each change is read and described. Layout tweaks, rotating banners and date stamps are left out, so what reaches you is a real change in content.

features.title: One brief on Mondays
features.body: The week's changes across every competitor in a watchlist, written up in plain sentences and sent by email and Slack.

features.title: No contract
features.body: Monthly plans at $29, $79 or $149, paid by card. Start today and cancel any time.

page.useCasesTitle: WebMonitor is the better fit if you

Want to know what competitors changed without someone curating a feed
Care most about pricing, product and hiring changes on competitor websites
Prefer a monthly plan you can cancel to an annual contract
page.limitsTitle: When Crayon is the better choice
page.limits: Choose Crayon if you need battlecards delivered inside Salesforce or Highspot, a CI program with reporting on how intel influences deals, coverage of news and reviews alongside websites, or win-loss tooling. WebMonitor only watches public web pages and has no CRM integration.

steps.title: Run a free snapshot

steps.title: Build a watchlist
steps.body: Add your main competitors. The suggested pages are usually all you need.

steps.title: Read the first brief
steps.body: Your first Monday brief arrives after a week of checks. Add rules for anything you need to hear about sooner.

faq.a: Crayon does not publish prices. Buyer data from Vendr shows contracts from about $12,700 to $46,000 a year, with a median around $30,000 and onboarding fees on top. WebMonitor is $29 to $149 a month.

faq.q: Does WebMonitor score how important a change is?
faq.a: WebMonitor reads each change and leaves out cosmetic ones, and each weekly brief opens with a headline naming the most important change of the week. It does not give each change a numeric score.

faq.q: Does WebMonitor track competitor news and reviews?
faq.a: It watches pages on the web, so a competitor's newsroom, blog or a public review page can be added. It does not pull from news wires or social networks.
There is one free competitor snapshot. Watchlists and the weekly brief are on paid plans from $29 a month.
